audit_status.source_base: Hebrew 1 Kings / Melakhim Aleph chapter 21, first-pass draft aligned to public-domain verse structure; formal legal, land-tenure, and reception-history audit remains required.
audit_status.review_note: Reviewed for ancestral land rights, royal purchase pressure, Ahab's entitlement, Jezebel's forged letters, religious fast as legal theater, false witnesses, capital punishment, state murder, land seizure, prophetic confrontation, corpse desecration, misogynistic scapegoating, repentance, restitution, and intergenerational punishment.

verses.restored: After these matters, Naboth the Jezreelite had a vineyard in Jezreel beside palace of Ahab king of Samaria.

familiar.text: And it came to pass after these things, that Naboth the Jezreelite had a vineyard, which was in Jezreel, hard by the palace of Ahab king of Samaria.

modern.text: Some time later, Naboth the Jezreelite happened to own a vineyard in Jezreel next to the palace of Ahab king of Samaria.

original.text: וַיְהִ֗י אַחַר֙ הַדְּבָרִ֣ים הָאֵ֔לֶּה כֶּ֧רֶם הָיָ֛ה לְנָב֥וֹת הַיִּזְרְעֵאלִ֖י אֲשֶׁ֣ר בְּיִזְרְעֶ֑אל אֵ֚צֶל הֵיכַ֣ל אַחְאָ֔ב מֶ֖לֶךְ שֹׁמְרֽוֹן

verses.restored: Ahab spoke to Naboth, saying, Give me your vineyard so it may be for me a vegetable garden, because it is near my house. I will give you in its place a better vineyard, or if good in your eyes, I will give you its price in silver.

familiar.text: And Ahab spake unto Naboth, saying, Give me thy vineyard, that I may have it for a garden of herbs, because it is near unto my house: and I will give thee for it a better vineyard than it; or, if it seem good to thee, I will give thee the worth of it in money.

modern.text: So Ahab said to Naboth, “Give me your vineyard to use as a vegetable garden, since it is next to my palace. I will give you a better vineyard in its place—or if you prefer, I will give you its value in silver.”

original.text: וַיְדַבֵּ֣ר אַחְאָ֣ב אֶל נָב֣וֹת לֵאמֹר֩ תְּנָה לִּ֨י אֶֽת כַּרְמְךָ֜ וִֽיהִי לִ֣י לְגַן יָרָ֗ק כִּ֣י ה֤וּא קָרוֹב֙ אֵ֣צֶל בֵּיתִ֔י וְאֶתְּנָ֤ה לְךָ֙ תַּחְתָּ֔יו כֶּ֖רֶם ט֣וֹב מִמֶּ֑נּוּ אִ֚ם ט֣וֹב בְּעֵינֶ֔יךָ אֶתְּנָה לְךָ֥ כֶ֖סֶף מְחִ֥יר זֶֽה

verses.restored: Naboth said to Ahab, Far be it from me by YHWH that I give inheritance of my ancestors to you.

familiar.text: And Naboth said to Ahab, The LORD forbid it me, that I should give the inheritance of my fathers unto thee.

modern.text: But Naboth replied, “The LORD forbid that I should give you the inheritance of my fathers.”

original.text: וַיֹּ֥אמֶר נָב֖וֹת אֶל אַחְאָ֑ב חָלִ֤ילָה לִּי֙ מֵֽיהוָ֔ה מִתִּתִּ֛י אֶת נַחֲלַ֥ת אֲבֹתַ֖י לָֽךְ

verses.restored: Ahab came to his house sullen and angry because of word Naboth the Jezreelite spoke: I will not give you inheritance of my ancestors. He lay upon bed, turned away his face, and ate no bread.

familiar.text: And Ahab came into his house heavy and displeased because of the word which Naboth the Jezreelite had spoken to him: for he had said, I will not give thee the inheritance of my fathers. And he laid him down upon his bed, and turned away his face, and would eat no bread.

modern.text: So Ahab went to his palace, sullen and angry because Naboth the Jezreelite had told him, “I will not give you the inheritance of my fathers.” He lay down on his bed, turned his face away, and refused to eat.

original.text: וַיָּבֹא֩ אַחְאָ֨ב אֶל בֵּית֜וֹ סַ֣ר וְזָעֵ֗ף עַל הַדָּבָר֙ אֲשֶׁר דִּבֶּ֣ר אֵלָ֗יו נָבוֹת֙ הַיִּזְרְעֵאלִ֔י וַיֹּ֕אמֶר לֹֽא אֶתֵּ֥ן לְךָ֖ אֶת נַחֲלַ֣ת אֲבוֹתָ֑י וַיִּשְׁכַּב֙ עַל מִטָּת֔וֹ וַיַּסֵּ֥ב אֶת פָּנָ֖יו וְלֹֽא אָ֥כַל לָֽחֶם

verses.restored: Jezebel his wife came to him and said, Why is your spirit sullen, and why do you not eat bread?

familiar.text: But Jezebel his wife came to him, and said unto him, Why is thy spirit so sad, that thou eatest no bread?

modern.text: Soon his wife Jezebel came in and asked, “Why are you so sullen that you refuse to eat?”

original.text: וַתָּבֹ֥א אֵלָ֖יו אִיזֶ֣בֶל אִשְׁתּ֑וֹ וַתְּדַבֵּ֣ר אֵלָ֗יו מַה זֶּה֙ רוּחֲךָ֣ סָרָ֔ה וְאֵינְךָ֖ אֹכֵ֥ל לָֽחֶם

verses.restored: He said to her, Because I spoke to Naboth the Jezreelite and said, Give me your vineyard for silver, or if you desire, I will give you another vineyard in its place. He said, I will not give you my vineyard.

familiar.text: And he said unto her, Because I spake unto Naboth the Jezreelite, and said unto him, Give me thy vineyard for money; or else, if it please thee, I will give thee another vineyard for it: and he answered, I will not give thee my vineyard.

modern.text: Ahab answered, “Because I spoke to Naboth the Jezreelite and told him, ‘Give me your vineyard for silver, or if you wish, I will give you another vineyard in its place.’ And he replied, ‘I will not give you my vineyard!’”

original.text: וַיְדַבֵּ֣ר אֵלֶ֗יהָ כִּֽי אֲ֠דַבֵּר אֶל נָב֨וֹת הַיִּזְרְעֵאלִ֜י וָאֹ֣מַר ל֗וֹ תְּנָה לִּ֤י אֶֽת כַּרְמְךָ֙ בְּכֶ֔סֶף א֚וֹ אִם חָפֵ֣ץ אַתָּ֔ה אֶתְּנָה לְךָ֥ כֶ֖רֶם תַּחְתָּ֑יו וַיֹּ֕אמֶר לֹֽא אֶתֵּ֥ן לְךָ֖ אֶת כַּרְמִֽי

verses.restored: Jezebel his wife said to him, You now exercise kingship over Israel? Arise, eat bread, and let your heart be good. I will give you vineyard of Naboth the Jezreelite.

familiar.text: And Jezebel his wife said unto him, Dost thou now govern the kingdom of Israel? arise, and eat bread, and let thine heart be merry: I will give thee the vineyard of Naboth the Jezreelite.

modern.text: But his wife Jezebel said to him, “Do you not reign over Israel? Get up, eat some food, and be cheerful, for I will get you the vineyard of Naboth the Jezreelite.” Jezebel’s Plot

original.text: וַתֹּ֤אמֶר אֵלָיו֙ אִיזֶ֣בֶל אִשְׁתּ֔וֹ אַתָּ֕ה עַתָּ֛ה תַּעֲשֶׂ֥ה מְלוּכָ֖ה עַל יִשְׂרָאֵ֑ל ק֤וּם אֱכָל לֶ֨חֶם֙ וְיִטַ֣ב לִבֶּ֔ךָ אֲנִי֙ אֶתֵּ֣ן לְךָ֔ אֶת כֶּ֖רֶם נָב֥וֹת הַיִּזְרְעֵאלִֽי

verses.restored: She wrote letters in Ahab's name, sealed them with his seal, and sent letters to elders and nobles living in Naboth's city.

familiar.text: So she wrote letters in Ahab’s name, and sealed them with his seal, and sent the letters unto the elders and to the nobles that were in his city, dwelling with Naboth.

modern.text: Then Jezebel wrote letters in Ahab’s name, sealed them with his seal, and sent them to the elders and nobles who lived with Naboth in his city.

original.text: וַתִּכְתֹּ֤ב סְפָרִים֙ בְּשֵׁ֣ם אַחְאָ֔ב וַתַּחְתֹּ֖ם בְּחֹתָמ֑וֹ וַתִּשְׁלַ֣ח הספרים אֶל הַזְקֵנִ֤ים וְאֶל הַֽחֹרִים֙ אֲשֶׁ֣ר בְּעִיר֔וֹ הַיֹּשְׁבִ֖ים אֶת נָבֽוֹת

verses.restored: She wrote in letters: Proclaim a fast and seat Naboth at head of people.

familiar.text: And she wrote in the letters, saying, Proclaim a fast, and set Naboth on high among the people:

modern.text: In the letters she wrote: “Proclaim a fast and give Naboth a seat of honor among the people.

original.text: וַתִּכְתֹּ֥ב בַּסְּפָרִ֖ים לֵאמֹ֑ר קִֽרְאוּ צ֔וֹם וְהוֹשִׁ֥יבוּ אֶת נָב֖וֹת בְּרֹ֥אשׁ הָעָֽם

verses.restored: Seat two worthless men before him, and let them testify against him, saying, You cursed Divine and king. Then take him out and stone him so he dies.

familiar.text: And set two men, sons of Belial, before him, to bear witness against him, saying, Thou didst blaspheme God and the king. And then carry him out, and stone him, that he may die.

modern.text: But seat two scoundrels opposite him and have them testify, ‘You have cursed both God and the king!’ Then take him out and stone him to death.”

original.text: וְ֠הוֹשִׁיבוּ שְׁנַ֨יִם אֲנָשִׁ֥ים בְּנֵֽי בְלִיַּעַל֮ נֶגְדּוֹ֒ וִיעִדֻ֣הוּ לֵאמֹ֔ר בֵּרַ֥כְתָּ אֱלֹהִ֖ים וָמֶ֑לֶךְ וְהוֹצִיאֻ֥הוּ וְסִקְלֻ֖הוּ וְיָמֹֽת

verses.restored: Men of his city—the elders and nobles living in his city—did as Jezebel sent to them, according to what was written in letters she sent.

familiar.text: And the men of his city, even the elders and the nobles who were the inhabitants in his city, did as Jezebel had sent unto them, and as it was written in the letters which she had sent unto them.

modern.text: So the elders and nobles who lived in Naboth’s city did as Jezebel had instructed in the letters she had written to them.

original.text: וַיַּעֲשׂוּ֩ אַנְשֵׁ֨י עִיר֜וֹ הַזְּקֵנִ֣ים וְהַחֹרִ֗ים אֲשֶׁ֤ר הַיֹּֽשְׁבִים֙ בְּעִיר֔וֹ כַּאֲשֶׁ֛ר שָׁלְחָ֥ה אֲלֵיהֶ֖ם אִיזָ֑בֶל כַּאֲשֶׁ֤ר כָּתוּב֙ בַּסְּפָרִ֔ים אֲשֶׁ֥ר שָׁלְחָ֖ה אֲלֵיהֶֽם

verses.restored: They proclaimed a fast and seated Naboth at head of people.

familiar.text: They proclaimed a fast, and set Naboth on high among the people.

modern.text: They proclaimed a fast and gave Naboth a seat of honor among the people.

original.text: קָרְא֖וּ צ֑וֹם וְהֹשִׁ֥יבוּ אֶת נָב֖וֹת בְּרֹ֥אשׁ הָעָֽם

verses.restored: Two worthless men came, sat before him, and testified against Naboth before people: Naboth cursed Divine and king. They took him outside city, stoned him with stones, and he died.

familiar.text: And there came in two men, children of Belial, and sat before him: and the men of Belial witnessed against him, even against Naboth, in the presence of the people, saying, Naboth did blaspheme God and the king. Then they carried him forth out of the city, and stoned him with stones, that he died.

modern.text: And the two scoundrels came in and sat opposite Naboth, and these men testified against him before the people, saying, “Naboth has cursed both God and the king!” So they took him outside the city and stoned him to death.

original.text: וַ֠יָּבֹאוּ שְׁנֵ֨י הָאֲנָשִׁ֥ים בְּנֵֽי בְלִיַּעַל֮ וַיֵּשְׁב֣וּ נֶגְדּוֹ֒ וַיְעִדֻהוּ֩ אַנְשֵׁ֨י הַבְּלִיַּ֜עַל אֶת נָב֗וֹת נֶ֤גֶד הָעָם֙ לֵאמֹ֔ר בֵּרַ֥ךְ נָב֛וֹת אֱלֹהִ֖ים וָמֶ֑לֶךְ וַיֹּצִאֻ֨הוּ֙ מִח֣וּץ לָעִ֔יר וַיִּסְקְלֻ֥הוּ בָאֲבָנִ֖ים וַיָּמֹֽת

verses.restored: They sent to Jezebel, saying, Naboth was stoned and is dead.

familiar.text: Then they sent to Jezebel, saying, Naboth is stoned, and is dead.

modern.text: Then they sent word to Jezebel: “Naboth has been stoned to death.”

original.text: וַֽיִּשְׁלְח֖וּ אֶל אִיזֶ֣בֶל לֵאמֹ֑ר סֻקַּ֥ל נָב֖וֹת וַיָּמֹֽת

verses.restored: When Jezebel heard Naboth was stoned and dead, she said to Ahab, Arise, possess vineyard of Naboth the Jezreelite, which he refused to give you for silver, for Naboth is not alive but dead.

familiar.text: And it came to pass, when Jezebel heard that Naboth was stoned, and was dead, that Jezebel said to Ahab, Arise, take possession of the vineyard of Naboth the Jezreelite, which he refused to give thee for money: for Naboth is not alive, but dead.

modern.text: When Jezebel heard that Naboth had been stoned to death, she said to Ahab, “Get up and take possession of the vineyard of Naboth the Jezreelite, who refused to give it to you for silver. For Naboth is no longer alive, but dead.”

original.text: וַֽיְהִי֙ כִּשְׁמֹ֣עַ אִיזֶ֔בֶל כִּֽי סֻקַּ֥ל נָב֖וֹת וַיָּמֹ֑ת וַתֹּ֨אמֶר אִיזֶ֜בֶל אֶל אַחְאָ֗ב ק֣וּם רֵ֞שׁ אֶת כֶּ֣רֶם נָב֣וֹת הַיִּזְרְעֵאלִ֗י אֲשֶׁ֤ר מֵאֵן֙ לָתֶת לְךָ֣ בְכֶ֔סֶף כִּ֣י אֵ֥ין נָב֛וֹת חַ֖י כִּי מֵֽת

verses.restored: When Ahab heard Naboth was dead, Ahab arose to go down to vineyard of Naboth the Jezreelite to possess it.

familiar.text: And it came to pass, when Ahab heard that Naboth was dead, that Ahab rose up to go down to the vineyard of Naboth the Jezreelite, to take possession of it.

modern.text: And when Ahab heard that Naboth was dead, he got up and went down to take possession of the vineyard of Naboth the Jezreelite. Elijah Denounces Ahab and Jezebel

original.text: וַיְהִ֛י כִּשְׁמֹ֥עַ אַחְאָ֖ב כִּ֣י מֵ֣ת נָב֑וֹת וַיָּ֣קָם אַחְאָ֗ב לָרֶ֛דֶת אֶל כֶּ֛רֶם נָב֥וֹת הַיִּזְרְעֵאלִ֖י לְרִשְׁתּֽוֹ

verses.restored: Word of YHWH came to Elijah the Tishbite, saying:

familiar.text: And the word of the LORD came to Elijah the Tishbite, saying,

modern.text: Then the word of the LORD came to Elijah the Tishbite, saying,

original.text: וַיְהִי֙ דְּבַר יְהוָ֔ה אֶל אֵלִיָּ֥הוּ הַתִּשְׁבִּ֖י לֵאמֹֽר

verses.restored: Arise, go down to meet Ahab king of Israel, who is in Samaria. Look, he is in vineyard of Naboth, where he went down to possess it.

familiar.text: Arise, go down to meet Ahab king of Israel, which is in Samaria: behold, he is in the vineyard of Naboth, whither he is gone down to possess it.

modern.text: “Get up and go down to meet Ahab king of Israel, who is in Samaria. See, he is in the vineyard of Naboth, of which he has gone to take possession.

original.text: ק֣וּם רֵ֗ד לִקְרַ֛את אַחְאָ֥ב מֶֽלֶךְ יִשְׂרָאֵ֖ל אֲשֶׁ֣ר בְּשֹׁמְר֑וֹן הִנֵּה֙ בְּכֶ֣רֶם נָב֔וֹת אֲשֶׁר יָ֥רַד שָׁ֖ם לְרִשְׁתּֽוֹ

verses.restored: Speak to him: Thus says YHWH, Have you murdered and also possessed? Then say: Thus says YHWH, In place where dogs licked blood of Naboth, dogs shall lick your blood—also yours.

familiar.text: And thou shalt speak unto him, saying, Thus saith the LORD, Hast thou killed, and also taken possession? And thou shalt speak unto him, saying, Thus saith the LORD, In the place where dogs licked the blood of Naboth shall dogs lick thy blood, even thine.

modern.text: Tell him that this is what the LORD says: ‘Have you not murdered a man and seized his land?’ Then tell him that this is also what the LORD says: ‘In the place where the dogs licked up the blood of Naboth, there also the dogs will lick up your blood—yes, yours!’ ”

original.text: וְדִבַּרְתָּ֨ אֵלָ֜יו לֵאמֹ֗ר כֹּ֚ה אָמַ֣ר יְהוָ֔ה הֲרָצַ֖חְתָּ וְגַם יָרָ֑שְׁתָּ וְדִבַּרְתָּ֨ אֵלָ֜יו לֵאמֹ֗ר כֹּ֚ה אָמַ֣ר יְהוָ֔ה בִּמְק֗וֹם אֲשֶׁ֨ר לָקְק֤וּ הַכְּלָבִים֙ אֶת דַּ֣ם נָב֔וֹת יָלֹ֧קּוּ הַכְּלָבִ֛ים אֶת דָּמְךָ֖ גַּם אָֽתָּה

verses.restored: Ahab said to Elijah, Have you found me, my enemy? He said, I found you, because you sold yourself to do evil in eyes of YHWH.

familiar.text: And Ahab said to Elijah, Hast thou found me, O mine enemy? And he answered, I have found thee: because thou hast sold thyself to work evil in the sight of the LORD.

modern.text: When Elijah arrived, Ahab said to him, “So you have found me out, my enemy.” He replied, “I have found you out because you have sold yourself to do evil in the sight of the LORD.

original.text: וַיֹּ֤אמֶר אַחְאָב֙ אֶל אֵ֣לִיָּ֔הוּ הַֽמְצָאתַ֖נִי אֹיְבִ֑י וַיֹּ֣אמֶר מָצָ֔אתִי יַ֚עַן הִתְמַכֶּרְךָ֔ לַעֲשׂ֥וֹת הָרַ֖ע בְּעֵינֵ֥י יְהוָֽה

verses.restored: Look, I am bringing evil upon you, sweeping away after you, and cutting off from Ahab every male—literally, one who urinates against wall—both restrained and abandoned in Israel.

familiar.text: Behold, I will bring evil upon thee, and will take away thy posterity, and will cut off from Ahab him that pisseth against the wall, and him that is shut up and left in Israel,

modern.text: This is what the LORD says: ‘I will bring calamity on you and consume your descendants; I will cut off from Ahab every male in Israel, both slave and free.

original.text: הִנְנִ֨י מבי אֵלֶ֨יךָ֙ רָעָ֔ה וּבִעַרְתִּ֖י אַחֲרֶ֑יךָ וְהִכְרַתִּ֤י לְאַחְאָב֙ מַשְׁתִּ֣ין בְּקִ֔יר וְעָצ֥וּר וְעָז֖וּב בְּיִשְׂרָאֵֽל

verses.restored: I will make your house like house of Jeroboam son of Nebat and house of Baasha son of Ahijah, because of provocation with which you provoked me and made Israel sin.

translation_notes: Naboth's vineyard is ancestral inheritance, not merely a commodity. His refusal protects family, identity, livelihood, and covenant land obligations against royal acquisition.
Ahab offers exchange or payment but responds to a lawful refusal with entitlement and withdrawal. A ruler's disappointment does not create a public need or right of seizure.

Jezebel uses Ahab's name, seal, local elders, a public fast, false witnesses, religious accusation, and execution law to manufacture legitimacy for murder. This is coordinated state and judicial corruption.
The local elders and nobles comply. Responsibility extends beyond Jezebel to every official, witness, executioner, beneficiary, and Ahab himself, who knowingly takes the land after Naboth's death.
The charge joins offense against Divine and king, showing how religion can be weaponized to protect political power and silence landholders.
Naboth is stoned outside the city. Capital punishment and public participation do not make false judgment just.
Elijah's question—Have you murdered and also possessed?—binds land seizure to the killing that made it possible. Restitution is conspicuously absent from Ahab's response.
Jezebel is individually accountable, but the chapter's phrasing has fueled misogynistic and xenophobic scapegoating. Ahab is king, seal owner, beneficiary, and active possessor.
Threats of dogs eating bodies and destruction of descendants are corpse desecration and collective punishment, not ethical justice.
Ahab's humility delays judgment to his son's generation. Repentance without restitution to Naboth's family remains incomplete, and transferring punishment to children is unjust.
safety_note: Do not use law, fasting, religious accusation, forged authority, or public consensus to seize land or silence dissent. Do not scapegoat Jezebel while excusing Ahab and collaborating officials. Center Naboth's land rights, due process, restitution, and protection from state violence; children must not inherit punishment.
